summary: Tested Product Intelligence Center end-to-end (backend aggregator + UI smoke). All 23 pytest cases pass against the live endpoint. Frontend smoke: anonymous gating, sidebar nav, full DOM presence of all 10 required data-testid sections, zero console errors. Idempotent batch seed verified by restarting the backend then re-asserting total batches == 45 (15 products * 3 batches).
critical_code_review_comments: product_intelligence.py is a single 675-line file; consider splitting AI brief + alert builders + heatmap fan-out into a `services/product_intel/` package to keep the router thin (~150 lines) and aid unit testing of pure helpers.

kpis.units_in_network.growth_pct uses a hardcoded 1.126 divisor to manufacture a fake prior-30d baseline because no historical inventory snapshot exists. This will silently show a stable +12.6% forever; either drop the field, mark `growth_pct: null`, or persist a daily inventory rollup so the delta is real. (Currently returns +12.6% in the live response.)

Geographic heatmap fans zone-level totals evenly across each zone's states (zone_units // n). This is documented but means per-state numbers are not real per-state numbers — they are zone averages duplicated. Acknowledged as a deliberate seed workaround; consider tagging retailers with real states in seed_csv so per-state colouring is truthful.

Batch '_days_left' is mutated on the in-memory dict and the status is re-derived live — good, but `_days_left` leaks into the response if any branch returns a batch directly. Currently safe because we only emit derived fields, but worth a quick `del b['_days_left']` before any future serialization.

expiry_risk.buckets uses en-dash labels (0–30 / 31–60 / 61–90). Tests use substring matches so this is OK, but the frontend hardcoded labels should match the dash style (en-dash) to avoid subtle UI mismatches.

ai_brief score top-up loop is +10 constant which pegs the demo manufacturer at 100/'Excellent' regardless of risk (verified live — score = 100 despite 'Knorr inventory nearing expiry' warning). Consider re-weighting so a 'risk' inventory state can actually drop the score below 100.
Recent_alerts timestamps are synthetic (now - 10m / 25m / 1h / 3h). For traceability swap with batch.created_at and a real audit/event log when one exists.
Active_batches KPI excludes recalled — good. But the spec says `>= 30`; current value is 39 (45 total - 6 expired). Healthy.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on critical paths (auth gate, sidebar link, 10/10 testids present, 0 console errors)
